newsitem.title: philippines: Philippine shares plunge 4.54 pct at close.
newsitem.headline: Philippine shares plunge 4.54 pct at close.

text.p: * Late-session technical buying lifts index above 2,700

The Philippine equities market suffered one of its heaviest losses in recent years as foreign investors triggered an across-the-board selldown on fears of poor first quarter corporate results, brokers said.
Fears of a property crash worsened the market's fears.
The composite index plunged by 128.87 points, or 4.54 percent, to 2,708.44 points at close, after falling to as low as 2,691.43 at midsession.
The fall is the biggest single-day drop in two years.
"The selling is tainted with emotions. It's already beyond reason," Rolly Pineda, vice president of Tower Securities, said.
Leading the losers were heavy-capitalised stocks such as Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co(PLDT), Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co, and Manila Electric Co.
PLDT was weighed down by its poor first quarter results. Other blue chips followed suit as their earning potentials have been put in doubt.
Fears of a property crash further exacerbated the selling. Leading the losers in the property sector was real estate giant Ayala Land Inc.
Pineda said the late-session buying was mostly due to technical buying and short-covering.
Only 15 stocks, mostly thirdliners, survived the bloodbath where 134 issues were severely battered. Turnover was heavy with about 3.5 billion pesos changing hands during the session.
Brokers expect the index to decline further in the coming days as negative sentiments persist. Pineda pegged the next support level at 2,650. -- RAMONCITO DELA CRUZ (63 2) 841-8939
